record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.context_brief: Regular null infinity from AF data
record.original_question: Determine conditions on asymptotically flat initial data that ensure the null infinity of the resulting Einstein initial-value evolution is regular enough for the Penrose extended manifold to exist with at least a C^3 metric and for the peeling theorem to hold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a four-dimensional manifold, with Cauchy initial data $(\Sigma, h, K)$ where $\Sigma$ is a smooth three-manifold, $h$ is a Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and $K$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor on $\Sigma$ satisfying the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations. Assume the data are asymptotically flat: there is a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset\Sigma$ such that $\Sigma\setminus\mathcal{K}$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\setminus B$ and, in the corresponding asymptotic coordinates $(x^i)$ with $r=|x|$,
$$h_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+O(r^{-1}),\qquad K_{ij}=O(r^{-2}),$$
together with appropriate decay of derivatives.

Let $(M,g)$ denote the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of $(\Sigma,h,K)$. Penrose's conformal compactification consists of finding a conformal factor $\Omega>0$ on $M$, with $\Omega\to 0$ suitably at infinity, so that $\tilde g=\Omega^{2}g$ extends to a manifold-with-boundary $\widetilde M=M\cup\mathscr{I}$ whose boundary $\mathscr{I}=\mathscr{I}^{+}\cup\mathscr{I}^{-}$ (future and past null infinity) carries a regular conformal metric. The peeling property asserts that, along outgoing null geodesics parametrized by an affine parameter $r$, the Weyl tensor components $\Psi_k$ ($k=0,1,2,3,4$) of the physical metric $g$ decay as $\Psi_k = O(r^{k-5})$ as $r\to\infty$ towards $\mathscr{I}^{+}$.

Problem. Determine explicit conditions on the asymptotically flat initial data $(\Sigma,h,K)$ which are sufficient (and, ideally, necessary) to guarantee that the maximal vacuum development $(M,g)$ admits a Penrose conformal extension $(\widetilde M,\tilde g)$ in which the extended metric $\tilde g$ is at least of class $C^{3}$ across $\mathscr{I}^{+}$, and in which the peeling decay of the Weyl tensor holds.
artifact.category_tag: Asymptotically flat spacetimes and null infinity
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been actively studied with substantial partial progress: Friedrich, Christodoulou–Klainerman, Chruściel–Delay, and others have given sufficient conditions on initial data (often involving conformally flat or symmetry conditions near spatial infinity, or specific decay/asymptotic-expansion hypotheses) yielding regular null infinity and peeling. A 2025 work ("From spatial to null infinity: Connecting initial data to peeling") gives further conditions on initial data ensuring peeling. Nevertheless, a complete characterization of the necessary and sufficient asymptotic conditions on general asymptotically flat data ensuring a $C^3$ Penrose extension and full peeling remains open.

status_evidence.title: From spatial to null infinity: Connecting initial data to peeling
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions on the initial data to obtain developments satisfying the peeling behavior... connections between peeling properties of the Weyl scalars and symmetries of initial data near spatial infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work providing partial conditions on initial data ensuring peeling; the precise general characterization remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic properties of the development of conformally flat data near spatial infinity
status_evidence.snippet: Friedrich's analysis of conformally flat data near spatial infinity and obstructions to smoothness of null infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Known obstructions (logarithmic terms) generically prevent smooth null infinity, showing only partial sufficient conditions are available.

status_evidence.title: The conformal approach to asymptotic analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Penrose conformal compactification, peeling, and conditions for regular null infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates the question of identifying sharp initial-data conditions for regular null infinity and peeling is a long-standing partially resolved problem.
